answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price admission with an ironclad bond: each new identity locks a ferrous stake before it may sign anything, so mass registration burns capital instead of printing trust. Reputation then accretes like an onyx, one thin honest layer per settled epoch, and peers verify depth band by band - a clone shows flat glass where the strata should be. Finally, every attestation must pass a fixed structural check, strict as a sonnet's meter: wrong counts, missing signatures, or duplicated hashes are rejected on the spot, making forgery expensive at every layer.
